subject: Materials Science
title: Miller Indices: Naming Crystal Planes
description: A short lesson to help you apply Miller Indices: Naming Crystal Planes.

hook.text: Crystals break along specific flat surfaces — cleavage planes — that repeat at the atomic level.

buildup.text: Miller indices (hkl) are three numbers that describe the orientation of a crystal plane.

discovery.text: Take the plane's intercepts on the axes, invert them, and clear fractions — that gives you (hkl).

twist.text: The (111) plane in an FCC metal is the most densely packed — and the most slippery for dislocation glide.

climax.text: Silicon wafers are cut on the (100) plane for optimal transistor performance — orientation matters.

punchline.text: Three little numbers tell you exactly how atoms line up on a plane.

quiz.question: What do Miller indices describe?
options: The temperature at which a crystal melts
The orientation of a plane within a crystal
The number of atoms in a unit cell
